questions.stem: Under which Article of the Constitution is the office of the Vice-President of India established?

options.option_text: Article 61
Article 63
Article 65
Article 68

questions.explanation: Article 63 states: 'There shall be a Vice-President of India.' Article 61 deals with impeachment of the President; Article 65 lays down the VP's role when the Presidency is vacant; Article 68 deals with the timing of elections to fill vacancies — all related but distinct articles.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Who elects the Vice-President of India?

options.option_text: An electoral college consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of State Legislative Assemblies
An electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament (both elected AND nominated)
Only the elected members of the Rajya Sabha
Direct election by universal adult franchise

questions.explanation: Article 66(1): The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college consisting of the members of BOTH Houses of Parliament — including both elected and nominated members. State legislators have no role. This is a narrower electoral college than the President's (which includes State Legislative Assembly members). Nominated members of RS/LS DO vote in VP elections (unlike in Presidential elections where only elected members vote).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following methods is used to elect the Vice-President of India?

options.option_text: First-past-the-post in a single round
Proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote, with voting by secret ballot
Open voting by show of hands
Voice vote in a joint session of Parliament

questions.explanation: Per Article 66(1), the VP is elected by proportional representation with single transferable vote by secret ballot. The same system (STV) is used for the President (Article 55) — this ensures a broad consensus; a candidate must secure a quota of first + transferred preferences to win.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a qualification for election as Vice-President of India?

options.option_text: Must be a citizen of India
Must have completed 35 years of age
Must be qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha
Must have held Ministerial office for at least 5 years before becoming eligible

questions.explanation: Article 66(3) lays down four qualifications: (a) citizen of India; (b) at least 35 years; (c) qualified for election as RS member; (d) not holding any office of profit under Union/State/local authority. There is no requirement of ministerial experience. Note the contrast with the President — a Presidential candidate must be qualified for election to the LOK Sabha, not the RS.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: What is the term of office of the Vice-President of India?

options.option_text: 4 years
5 years
6 years
Co-terminus with the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Article 67: The VP holds office for a term of 5 years from the date he enters upon office. He is eligible for re-election any number of times. The tenure is NOT tied to the Lok Sabha. Note: 6 years is the term of Rajya Sabha members and CAG — a common distractor.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio:

options.option_text: Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
Chairman of the Inter-State Council
Chairman of the Planning Commission

questions.explanation: Article 64: The VP is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. He presides over RS sittings, has a casting vote in case of a tie, and draws salary as Chairman of the RS. The Speaker of the LS is a separate elected position (Article 93). The Planning Commission was dissolved in 2014 and replaced by NITI Aayog (chaired by the PM, not the VP).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: How is the Vice-President of India removed from office?

options.option_text: By impeachment, following the same procedure as the President
By a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by an effective majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha
By the Supreme Court after a reference by the President
By the Electoral College that elected him, through a recall vote

questions.explanation: Article 67(b): The VP can be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by an EFFECTIVE MAJORITY (i.e., a majority of all the then members of the RS) AND agreed to by a simple majority in the Lok Sabha. A 14-day prior notice is required. This is LESS STRINGENT than Presidential impeachment (which requires a two-thirds majority in each House). The VP's removal has never been invoked in practice.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: When the office of the President falls vacant due to death, resignation, removal, or otherwise, the Vice-President acts as President. What is the maximum period for which he can do so?

options.option_text: Until a new President is elected, but no more than 6 months
Until the next general election
1 year
Till the remainder of the original President's term

questions.explanation: Article 65(1) + Article 62: When the Presidency falls vacant, the VP acts as President. An election to fill the vacancy must be held as soon as possible and, in any case, within 6 months of the vacancy. The VP's acting tenure is thus capped at 6 months, after which a regularly elected President must take over. V. V. Giri acted as President after Zakir Hussain's death in 1969 until his own election as President.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Who was the first Vice-President of India?

options.option_text: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
Dr. S. Radhakrishnan
Dr. Zakir Hussain
V. V. Giri

questions.explanation: Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan was the first Vice-President (1952–62) and later became the second President (1962–67). Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first PRESIDENT, not VP — a classic confusion. Dr. Zakir Hussain was the second VP (1962–67) before becoming the third President. V. V. Giri was the fourth VP.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the salary of the Vice-President is correct?

options.option_text: He draws a fixed salary as Vice-President that is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
He draws no salary as Vice-President; he receives salary as Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
He draws salary as Vice-President from the Contingency Fund of India
He draws salary partly from the Rajya Sabha and partly from the President's fund

questions.explanation: The Constitution (Article 97) provides the VP receives NO separate salary for being VP — he draws salary in his capacity as Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. This salary is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India (non-votable). This peculiar arrangement is because the VP has no executive duties of his own; his primary role is presiding over the RS.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: When the Vice-President is acting as President, who performs the duties of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?

options.option_text: The Prime Minister, as Leader of the House
The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
A member elected by the Rajya Sabha for this purpose

questions.explanation: Article 91: When the VP acts as or discharges the functions of the President, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (or, in his absence, any other member of the RS authorised by the President) performs the duties of the Chairman of the RS. The VP CANNOT simultaneously chair the RS while acting as President.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The oath of office to the Vice-President is administered by:

options.option_text: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chief Justice of India
The President of India (or in his absence, a person appointed in that behalf by him)
The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: Article 69: The VP's oath is administered by the President or some person appointed in that behalf by him. This is distinct from the President's oath — which is administered by the Chief Justice of India (Article 60). Many students confuse the two; the CJI administers the oath of the President, NOT the Vice-President.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: If a dispute arises regarding the election of the Vice-President, to which body does the Constitution assign jurisdiction to decide it?

options.option_text: The Election Commission of India
The President, after consultation with the Council of Ministers
The Supreme Court of India, with its decision being final
The joint sitting of Parliament

questions.explanation: Article 71(1): All doubts and disputes arising out of or in connection with the election of the President or the Vice-President shall be inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court, whose decision is FINAL. The ECI conducts the election but doesn't decide disputes. Note that even if the election is later declared void, acts done by the VP in the meantime are NOT invalidated (Article 71(2)).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following is a difference between the election of the President and the Vice-President of India?

options.option_text: Members of State Legislative Assemblies vote in the Presidential election but not in the Vice-Presidential election
The President is elected by secret ballot, but the VP is elected by open ballot
The VP is elected by a simple majority, the President by a two-thirds majority
Only the President's election is held by proportional representation

questions.explanation: Key difference: The Presidential electoral college includes elected MPs + elected MLAs of State Assemblies (Article 54). The VP electoral college includes ONLY MPs (elected + nominated) of both Houses of Parliament — no MLAs (Article 66). Both use STV with secret ballot; both use proportional representation. Majority requirements are computed by quota, not by simple/two-thirds.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which among the following Vice-Presidents did NOT go on to become the President of India?

options.option_text: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan
Dr. Zakir Hussain
Krishan Kant
R. Venkataraman

questions.explanation: Krishan Kant served as the 10th Vice-President (1997–2002) and died in office before being elevated. He is the only VP to die while in office. Dr. Radhakrishnan, Dr. Zakir Hussain, V. V. Giri, R. Venkataraman, Shankar Dayal Sharma, and K. R. Narayanan all went on to become President. Seven of India's first thirteen Presidents were previously VPs — making this a historical pattern the question tests.
